title: The swimming pool till
instruction: Children under 15 and people aged 65 and over get a discount. The till decides by a program. Step through it for everyone who comes.
debrief: A condition decides exactly, even at the edge: a 15-year-old no longer gets the discount, a 65-year-old does. Edges and mixing up “and” with “or” are where conditions most often go wrong.

steps.q: Which ticket does the till print?
steps.why: 9 < 15 holds. With “or”, one true part is enough.

steps.q: Which ticket does the till print?
steps.why: Watch the edge: 15 < 15 does not hold. And 15 ≥ 65 doesn't either.

steps.q: Which ticket does the till print?
Which ticket does the till print?
steps.why: ≥ means “greater than or equal to”. 65 ≥ 65 holds.

steps.q: Which ticket does the till print?
Which ticket does Karel get now?
steps.why: 65 > 65 doesn't hold. Karel pays full price even though he should get the discount. The mistake is a single character: it should be ≥.

steps.q: Someone wrote “and” instead of “or”. Who gets the discount now?
steps.why: Nobody can be under 15 and 65 or older at the same time. With “and” both parts must hold, so the condition never does.
